question: At the frozen 200-season natural near/far bridge, does deterministic density mass approximate the finite-ABM population scale?
verification: reproduce prior finite mean far-minus-near effect near -0.1446
reproduce prior deterministic mean far-minus-near effect near -0.4510
verify deterministic endpoint is invariant across demographic replicate within history/start/arm

interpretation_rule.strong_scale_disagreement: finite far occupancy is 1.0 while median deterministic far density mass is <1 and paired finite mean population is orders of magnitude larger
interpretation_rule.consequence: do not interpret ABM-versus-density trait difference or capacity movement toward density as a pure finite-population attenuation or convergence to a stochastic expectation

claim_boundary: This is a diagnostic rerun of already inspected frozen bridge conditions, not a fresh confirmatory experiment.
The diagnostic tests population-scale comparability of two model layers; it does not change biological parameters or select histories.
The deterministic genotype-density implementation is documented in code as a conditional deterministic closure, not the stochastic mean.
All 128 histories, three starts, eight demographic repeats, and both natural arms are retained.
